questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 18 minutes, while pipe B can empty the completely filled tank in 20 minutes. Initially, pipe A is opened and after 6 minutes pipe B is also opened. In how much time (in minutes) will the remaining tank be filled completely?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity of the tank = LCM(18, 20) = 180 units.

Efficiency of Pipe A = +10 units/min and Efficiency of Pipe B = −9 units/min.

Tank filled by Pipe A in the first 6 minutes = 6 × 10 = 60 units.

Remaining capacity to fill = 180 − 60 = 120 units.

Time to fill remaining part = 120 ÷ (10 − 9) = 120 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Time taken by Pipe A to fill the tank = 18 minutes

⇒ Time taken by Pipe B to empty the tank = 20 minutes

⇒ Time for which only Pipe A was operated initially = 6 minutes

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Total Work = LCM of individual time taken

⇒ Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

⇒ Time Required = Remaining Work ÷ Net Combined Efficiency

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time**
 **Total Capacity**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A (Fills)
 18 mins
 180 units
 +10 units/min
 
 

 B (Empties)
 20 mins
 −9 units/min
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In the first 6 minutes, work done by Pipe A = 6 × 10 = 60 units.

⇒ Remaining capacity to be filled = 180 − 60 = 120 units.

⇒ After 6 minutes, both pipes A and B are open together.

⇒ Net efficiency of both pipes combined = 10 + (−9) = +1 unit/min.

⇒ Time required to fill the remaining capacity = 120 units ÷ 1 unit/min = 120 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Net Efficiency

When a filling pipe (time x) and an emptying pipe (time y) run together, the net part filled per hour is (1/x − 1/y), provided the filling rate is higher than the emptying rate.

Concept of Leakage

A leakage at the bottom of a tank acts exactly like an emptying pipe. It continuously reduces the effective efficiency of the filling pipes, thereby increasing the total time required to completely fill the tank.

Alternating Pipes Method

When filling and emptying pipes are opened in alternate turns, compute the net work done in a full cycle (e.g., 2 hours). Special care must be taken towards the end, as the tank might become completely filled before the next emptying cycle begins.
</p

questions.question: Varun and Ashish together can paint a hall in 3 days. Varun alone can paint it in 7 days. In how many days can Ashish alone paint 4 such halls?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let total work for 1 hall be LCM(3, 7) = 21 units.

Combined efficiency of Varun and Ashish = 21 ÷ 3 = 7 units/day.

Varun's efficiency = 21 ÷ 7 = 3 units/day.

Ashish's efficiency = 7 − 3 = 4 units/day.

Time required for Ashish to paint 4 halls = (4 × 21) ÷ 4 = 21 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 21 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Varun and Ashish together to paint 1 hall = 3 days

Time taken by Varun alone to paint 1 hall = 7 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of individual days

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken

Total Time = Total Work ÷ Efficiency

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Varun + Ashish
 3
 21
 21 ÷ 3 = 7
 
 

 Varun
 7
 21 ÷ 7 = 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of Ashish = Efficiency of (Varun + Ashish) − Efficiency of Varun

⇒ Efficiency of Ashish = 7 − 3 = 4 units/day

⇒ Total work to paint 4 such halls = 4 × 21 = 84 units

⇒ Time taken by Ashish alone to paint 4 halls = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of Ashish

⇒ Time taken by Ashish = 84 ÷ 4 = 21 days

**∴ The correct answer is 21 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

Works exactly like Time & Work. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency, while outlet pipes (leaks) have negative efficiency.

Work and Wages

Wages are strictly distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each person. If they work for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Days Work

When people work on alternate days, calculate the total work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people) and divide the total work by the cycle work to find the number of cycles required.
</p

questions.question: Two pipes, A and B, can fill a tank of 3700 litres in 9 hours and 6 hours, respectively. If they are opened together, how many hours will they take to fill an empty tank of 6400 litres?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency of **Pipe A** = 3700 ÷ 9 litres/hr.

Efficiency of **Pipe B** = 3700 ÷ 6 litres/hr.

Combined efficiency = (3700 × (2 + 3)) ÷ 18 = (3700 × 5) ÷ 18 = 18500 ÷ 18 = 9250 ÷ 9 litres/hr.

Time to fill 6400 litres = 6400 ÷ (9250 ÷ 9) = (6400 × 9) ÷ 9250 = (640 × 9) ÷ 925 = 1152 ÷ 185 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1152/185 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 **Pipe**
 **Time (hrs)**
 **Reference Work (litres)**
 **Efficiency (litres/hr)**

 **A**
 9
 3700
 3700 ÷ 9

 **B**
 6
 3700 ÷ 6

**Total Capacity** of target tank = 6400 litres.

⇒ Efficiency of **Pipe A** (EA) = 3700/9 litres/hr.

⇒ Efficiency of **Pipe B** (EB) = 3700/6 = 1850/3 litres/hr.

⇒ Combined Efficiency (EA₊B) = (3700/9) + (1850/3) = (3700 + 5550)/9 = 9250/9 litres/hr.

⇒ Time taken = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time = 6400 ÷ (9250/9) = (6400 × 9) ÷ 9250

⇒ Time = (640 × 9) ÷ 925 = 5760 ÷ 925

⇒ Time = 1152/185 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1152/185 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Efficiency Formula

When two pipes work together, their **total efficiency** is the sum of their individual efficiencies: Eₜₒₜₐₗ = E₁ + E₂.

Time and Work Relationship

The **time** taken to complete a task is inversely proportional to the **efficiency**: Time = Total Work ÷ Efficiency.

Inlet vs Outlet Pipes

**Inlet pipes** have positive efficiency (add water), while **outlet pipes** (leaks) have negative efficiency (remove water).</p

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 10 minutes while another pipe can empty completely filled tank in 20 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill the tank completely?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net work per minute = (1 ÷ **filling time**) − (1 ÷ **emptying time**)

Net filling rate = (1 ÷ 10) − (1 ÷ 20) = 1 ÷ 20

Time taken = **Reciprocal** of net rate = 20 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 20 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 **Pipe Type**
 **Time (min)**
 **Total Capacity (LCM)**
 **Efficiency**

 **Inlet Pipe**
 10
 20 units
 +2

 **Outlet Pipe**
 20
 −1

⇒ **Combined Efficiency** = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/min

⇒ **Time required** = Total Capacity ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time = 20 ÷ 1 = 20 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 20 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Rule

Work done by an **inlet pipe** is always considered positive, while work done by an **outlet (leak)** is negative.

Total Capacity (LCM Method)

The **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the individual times provides the most convenient value for total tank capacity.

Net Time Formula

If pipe A fills in 'x' and pipe B empties in 'y' (y > x), time taken together = (x × y) ÷ (y − x).</p

questions.question: Two pipes, A and B, can fill a tank of 7800 litres in 12 hours and 10 hours, respectively. If they are opened together, how many hours will they take to fill an empty tank of 8800 litres?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Rate of **Pipe A** = 7800 ÷ 12 = 650 litres/hr

Rate of **Pipe B** = 7800 ÷ 12 = 780 litres/hr

Combined Rate = 650 + 780 = 1430 litres/hr

Time to fill 8800 litres = 8800 ÷ 1430 = 880 ÷ 143 = 80/13 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 80/13 hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Capacity 1 = 7800 litres, Time A = 12 hrs, Time B = 10 hrs, Target Capacity = 8800 litres.

**Formula Used:** Efficiency = Work ÷ Time; Time = Work ÷ Total Efficiency

 **Pipe**
 **Time (hrs)**
 **Base Work (litres)**
 **Efficiency (litres/hr)**

 **A**
 12
 7800
 650

 **B**
 10
 780

⇒ Total Efficiency (A + B) = 650 + 780 = 1430 litres/hr

⇒ Target Work = 8800 litres

⇒ Required Time = 8800 ÷ 1430

⇒ Required Time = 880/143

⇒ Required Time = (80 × 11) ÷ (13 × 11) = 80/13 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 80/13 hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time when work is constant. If an **inlet pipe** fills a tank in 'x' hours, its work done in 1 hour is 1/x.

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

**Inlet pipes** perform positive work while **outlet pipes** (leakage) perform negative work. Net efficiency = Σ(Inlet Efficiency) − Σ(Outlet Efficiency).

Combined Work Formula

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B in y hours, they together fill in (x × y) ÷ (x + y) hours for the **same total work**.</p

questions.question: Robin and Varun together can paint a hall in 6 days. Robin alone can paint it in 42 days. In how many days can Varun alone paint it?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Days for **Varun** = (Product of days) ÷ (Difference of days)

Days for **Varun** = (42 × 6) ÷ (42 − 6)

Days for **Varun** = 252 ÷ 36 = 7 days

**∴ The correct answer is 7 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **Robin + Varun** = 6 days

Time taken by **Robin** alone = 42 days

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 **Robin + Varun** 6 42 7 
 **Robin** 42 1 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of **Varun** = (Efficiency of **Robin + Varun**) − (Efficiency of **Robin**)

⇒ Efficiency of **Varun** = 7 − 1 = 6 units/day

⇒ Time taken by **Varun** = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of **Varun**

⇒ Time taken by **Varun** = 42 ÷ 6 = 7 days

**∴ The correct answer is 7 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Combined Work Formula

If A takes 'a' days and B takes 'b' days, together they take (a × b) / (a + b) days.

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

Individual Work Calculation

If (A+B) take T days and A takes 'a' days, then B takes (T × a) / (a − T) days.</p

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 21 minutes while another pipe can empty completely filled tank in 24 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill one-fourth of the tank?

⇒ **One-fourth of Tank Capacity** = 168 ÷ 4 = 42 units

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Efficiency of an **inlet pipe** is always positive, whereas the efficiency of an **outlet (emptying) pipe** is always negative.

Work and Efficiency Relation

Time taken = **Total Work** ÷ **Net Efficiency**. If net efficiency is positive, the tank fills; if negative, the tank empties.</p

questions.question: A and B can do a job in 25 days and 18 days, respectively. A works alone for 4 days and leaves. The number of days required by B to complete the remaining job is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work (LCM of 25, 18) = 450 units

Efficiency: A = 18 units/day, B = 25 units/day

Work done by A in 4 days = 18 × 4 = 72 units

Remaining work = 450 − 72 = 378 units

Days taken by B = 378 ÷ 25 = 15 (3/25) days

**∴ The correct answer is 15 (3/25) days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **A** = 25 days, Time taken by **B** = 18 days. **A** worked for 4 days.

**Formula Used:** Work = Efficiency × Time; Remaining Work = Total Work − Work Done.

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**

 **A**
 25
 450
 18

 **B**
 18
 25

⇒ Total Work = LCM(25, 18) = 450 units

⇒ Work completed by **A** in 4 days = 18 × 4 = 72 units

⇒ Remaining Work = 450 − 72 = 378 units

⇒ Days required by **B** = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Days = 378 ÷ 25

⇒ Days = 15 (3/25) days

**∴ The correct answer is 15 (3/25) days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken to complete a job. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

Remaining Work Concept

When a person leaves, the **Remaining Work** must be divided by the **Efficiency** of the person staying to find the additional time required.

LCM Method

Using the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the given days as the total work simplifies calculation by avoiding fractions until the final step.</p

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 9 minutes while another pipe can empty completely filled tank in 90 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill half of the tank?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net filling rate = 1/9 − 1/90 = (10 − 1)/90 = 9/90 = 1/10 per minute.

Time to fill the **full tank** = 10 minutes.

Time to fill **half of the tank** = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Filling pipe (A) time = 9 minutes

Emptying pipe (B) time = 90 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of time taken

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 **Pipe** **Time (min)** **Total Work (units)** **Efficiency** 
 A (Inlet) 9 90 +10 
 B (Outlet) 90 −1 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Combined efficiency of (A + B) = 10 − 1 = 9 units/min

⇒ Total work to fill half tank = 90 ÷ 2 = 45 units

⇒ Time taken = 45 ÷ 9 = 5 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 5 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Net Work Done

When one pipe fills and another empties, the net efficiency is the difference: (1/x − 1/y).

Pipes and Cisterns Logic

Inlet pipes have positive efficiency, while outlet (leakage) pipes have negative efficiency.

Fractional Work

To find the time for a fraction of work, multiply the total time required for full work by that fraction.</p

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 18 minutes, while pipe B can empty the completely filled tank in 27 minutes. Initially, pipe A is opened and after 6 minutes pipe B is also opened. In how much time (in minutes) will the remaining tank be filled completely?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let **Total Work** (LCM of 18, 27) = 54 units.

**Efficiency** of **Pipe A** = +3, **Efficiency** of **Pipe B** = −2.

Work done by **Pipe A** in 6 minutes = 3 × 6 = 18 units.

Remaining work = 54 − 18 = 36 units.

Combined efficiency (A + B) = 3 − 2 = 1 unit/min.

Time for remaining part = 36 ÷ 1 = 36 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time of **Pipe A** = 18 min; Emptying time of **Pipe B** = 27 min.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Time × Efficiency

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 Pipe A (Fill) 18 54 3 
 Pipe B (Empty) 27 −2 

⇒ Work done by **Pipe A** alone for first 6 minutes = 6 × 3 = 18 units.

⇒ Remaining capacity to be filled = 54 − 18 = 36 units.

⇒ When both pipes are open, net efficiency = 3 + (−2) = 1 unit/min.

⇒ Time taken to fill the remaining tank = 36 ÷ 1 = 36 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Rule

An **inlet pipe** has positive efficiency while an **outlet pipe** (leak) has negative efficiency.

Net Efficiency

If two pipes fill/empty at rates x and y, combined rate = (x ± y) depending on the nature of the pipes.

Total Capacity

The **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of individual times provides a convenient assumption for total tank capacity.</p

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 9 minutes while another pipe can empty completely filled tank in 90 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill the tank completely?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net filling time = (**a × b**) ÷ (**b − a**), where a is filling time and b is emptying time.

Net time = (9 × 90) ÷ (90 − 9)

Net time = 810 ÷ 81 = 10 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 
 **Pipe Type** **Time (min)** **Total Work (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 Filling Pipe 9 90 units +10 
 Emptying Pipe 90 −1 

⇒ **Combined Efficiency** = 10 − 1 = 9 units/minute.

⇒ **Time taken to fill tank** = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time = 90 ÷ 9 = 10 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency

Efficiency of a **filling pipe** is taken as **positive (+)**, while the efficiency of an **emptying pipe (leak)** is taken as **negative (−)**.

Net Work Formula

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B empties in y hours, the net work in 1 hour is (1/x − 1/y). If the result is positive, the tank is **filling**; if negative, the tank is **emptying**.</p

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 9 minutes, while pipe B can empty the completely filled tank in 10 minutes. Initially, pipe A is opened and after 3 minutes pipe B is also opened. In how much time (in minutes) will the remaining tank be filled completely?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let **Total Capacity** of the tank be **LCM(9, 10) = 90 units**.

Efficiency of **Pipe A** = 90 ÷ 9 = 10 units/min (Filling).

Efficiency of **Pipe B** = 90 ÷ 10 = −9 units/min (Emptying).

Work done by **Pipe A** in first 3 minutes = 10 × 3 = 30 units.

Remaining work = 90 − 30 = 60 units.

Combined efficiency (A + B) = 10 − 9 = 1 unit/min.

Remaining time = 60 ÷ 1 = 60 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 60 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time of **Pipe A** = 9 mins; Emptying time of **Pipe B** = 10 mins; **A** works alone for 3 mins.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Efficiency × Time; Net Efficiency = Filling Efficiency − Emptying Efficiency.

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 Pipe A 9 90 10 
 Pipe B 10 −9 

⇒ Work completed by **Pipe A** in 3 mins = 10 × 3 = 30 units

⇒ Remaining Capacity = 90 − 30 = 60 units

⇒ Combined Efficiency of (A + B) = 10 + (−9) = 1 unit/min

⇒ Time to fill remaining tank = Remaining Capacity ÷ Net Efficiency

⇒ Time = 60 ÷ 1 = 60 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 60 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Sign Convention

Always take the efficiency of a **filling pipe** as positive (+) and an **emptying pipe** (leakage) as negative (−).

Net Efficiency Formula

If pipe A fills in 'x' hours and pipe B empties in 'y' hours, the part filled in 1 hour while both are open is (1/x − 1/y).

Total Capacity Calculation

The easiest way to find the tank capacity is to calculate the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the individual times given.</p

questions.question: A water tank can be filled in 29 minutes by using 23 pipes of the same capacity. In how many minutes (rounded off to two decimal places) will the water tank be filled if we use 47 pipes of the same capacity as above?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Apply the **Inverse Proportion** rule: **M₁ × T₁ = M₂ × T₂**

Here, **23 pipes × 29 minutes = 47 pipes × Time**

Time = (23 × 29) ÷ 47 = 667 ÷ 47

Time ≈ 14.19 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 14.19 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of pipes (**M₁**) = 23

Initial time (**T₁**) = 29 minutes

Final number of pipes (**M₂**) = 47

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Number of Pipes × Time taken

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total capacity of tank = 23 × 29 units

⇒ Total capacity = 667 units

⇒ Time taken by 47 pipes = Total capacity ÷ Number of pipes

⇒ Time = 667 ÷ 47

⇒ Time = 14.19148...

⇒ Time ≈ 14.19 minutes (rounded off to two decimal places)

**∴ The correct answer is 14.19 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Variation

In **Pipes and Cisterns**, the number of pipes is inversely proportional to the time taken to fill the tank (if all pipes have the same efficiency).

Chain Rule Formula

The general formula is M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂, where M is efficiency/pipes, D is days/minutes, and W is work/capacity.</p

questions.question: A can lay a railway track between two given stations in 8 days and B can do the same job in 24 days. With the help of C, they can do the job in 3 days. C alone can do the job in:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = **LCM(8, 24, 3) = 24 units**.

Efficiency of **A = 3**, **B = 1**, and **(A + B + C) = 8**.

Efficiency of **C = 8 − (3 + 1) = 4**.

Time taken by **C = 24 ÷ 4 = 6 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **A = 8 days**, **B = 24 days**, and **(A + B + C) = 3 days**.

 **Person**

 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**

 **A**
 8
 24
 3

 **B**
 24
 1

 **A + B + C**
 3
 8

⇒ Efficiency of **C** = Efficiency of **(A + B + C)** − Efficiency of **A** − Efficiency of **B**

⇒ Efficiency of **C** = 8 − 3 − 1 = 4 units/day

⇒ Time taken by **C** = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of **C**

⇒ Time taken by **C** = 24 ÷ 4 = 6 days

**∴ The correct answer is 6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work Formula

**Total Work** is always considered as the **LCM** of the individual number of days to simplify efficiency calculations.

Efficiency Relationship

**Efficiency** is inversely proportional to **Time**. If time increases, efficiency decreases for the same amount of work (E = W ÷ T).

Combined Work

If individuals work together, their **efficiencies** are added to find the combined rate of work per day.</p

questions.question: 9 men or 8 women can do a job in 19 days. 9 men work for 9 days and leave. The number of women required to complete the remaining work in 8 days is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total work in terms of **men-days** = 9 × 19 = 171 units.

Work done by 9 men in 9 days = 9 × 9 = 81 units.

Remaining work = 171 − 81 = 90 units (to be done by women).

Since 9 men = 8 women, 171 men-days = 8 × 19 = 152 women-days.

Ratio of Men work to Women work is 8 : 9. Remaining work for women = 90 × (8/9) = 80 women-days.

Number of women needed for 8 days = 80 ÷ 8 = 10 women.

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 9 Men 19 8 
 8 Women 19 152 8 

**Given:** 9 men or 8 women can do a job in 19 days.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Efficiency of 9 men = 152 ÷ 19 = 8 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of 8 women = 152 ÷ 19 = 8 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of 1 woman = 8 ÷ 8 = 1 unit/day

⇒ Work done by 9 men in 9 days = 8 × 9 = 72 units

⇒ Remaining work = 152 − 72 = 80 units

⇒ Women required to finish 80 units in 8 days = 80 ÷ (8 × 1) = 10 women

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

**__Additional Information__**

The 'OR' Concept in Work

When a question says 'A or B', it implies that the total capacity of group A is equal to the total capacity of group B (m₁d₁ = m₂d₂).

Work & Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken. If the same work is done in fewer days, the efficiency of the group must be higher.

Man-Day Formula

M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂, where M is number of workers, D is days, H is hours, and W is work.</p

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 57 hours, B and C together can do it in 28 hours, while A and C together can do it in 19 hours. How long (in hours) will B alone take to do it?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
**Total Work** (LCM of 57, 28, 19) = 1596 units.

Efficiency of **A** = 1596 ÷ 57 = 28 units/hr.

Efficiency of **A + C** = 1596 ÷ 19 = 84 units/hr → Efficiency of **C** = 84 − 28 = 56 units/hr.

Efficiency of **B + C** = 1596 ÷ 28 = 57 units/hr → Efficiency of **B** = 57 − 56 = 1 unit/hr.

Time taken by **B** = 1596 ÷ 1 = 1596 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1596 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **A** = 57 hours

Time taken by **B + C** = 28 hours

Time taken by **A + C** = 19 hours

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency**
 **A** 57 1596 28
 **B + C** 28 57
 **A + C** 19 84
**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of **A** = 28

⇒ Efficiency of **A + C** = 84

⇒ Efficiency of **C** = (A + C) − A = 84 − 28 = 56

⇒ Efficiency of **B + C** = 57

⇒ Efficiency of **B** = (B + C) − C = 57 − 56 = 1

⇒ Time taken by **B alone** = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time = 1596 ÷ 1 = 1596 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 1596 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Combined Efficiency

When multiple people work together, their **individual efficiencies** are added to find the total rate of work per unit time.

Total Work Assumption

Taking the **LCM (Least Common Multiple)** of the given time durations as the total work simplifies calculations by ensuring efficiencies are integers.

Inverse Relationship

For a constant amount of work, **Time** is inversely proportional to **Efficiency** (T ∝ 1/E).</p

questions.question: 2 men or 9 women can do a job in 14 days. 2 men work for 9 days and leave. The number of women required to complete the remaining work in 9 days is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency ratio **M : W** ⇒ **2M = 9W** ⇒ **M/W = 9/2**.

Total Work = **2 × 9 × 14 = 252 units**.

Work done by **2 men** in **9 days** = **2 × 9 × 9 = 162 units**.

Remaining Work = **252 − 162 = 90 units**.

Women required (**n**) × Efficiency (**2**) × Days (**9**) = **90** ⇒ **n = 90 ÷ 18 = 5**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 women.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 2 Men (M) = 9 Women (W) can complete work in 14 days.

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 2 Men 14 18 units/day 
 9 Women 14 252 units 18 units/day 

⇒ Efficiency of **1 Man** = **18 ÷ 2 = 9 units/day**.

⇒ Efficiency of **1 Woman** = **18 ÷ 9 = 2 units/day**.

⇒ Work done by **2 men** in **9 days** = **(2 × 9) × 9 = 162 units**.

⇒ Remaining work = **252 − 162 = 90 units**.

⇒ Time allowed for remaining work = **9 days**.

⇒ Required efficiency = **90 ÷ 9 = 10 units/day**.

⇒ Number of women = **Required efficiency ÷ Efficiency of 1 woman**.

⇒ Number of women = **10 ÷ 2 = 5**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 women.**

**__Additional Information__**

The 'OR' Concept

When **M₁** men OR **W₁** women can do a job, equate their total work capacities: **M₁ × Days = W₁ × Days** to find the efficiency ratio.

Work-Efficiency Formula

Total Work = **Efficiency × Time**. If work is constant, Efficiency is inversely proportional to Time.

M-D-H Rule

For different groups, use **(M₁×D₁×H₁)/W₁ = (M₂×D₂×H₂)/W₂** where M is persons, D is days, H is hours, and W is work.</p

questions.question: Two pipes can fill a cistern, individually, in 35 min and 15 min, respectively. There is a pipe located at the bottom of the cistern to empty it. If all the three pipes are opened simultaneously, then the empty cistern gets filled in 42 min. How long will the pipe at the bottom of the cistern take to empty the completely filled cistern if no other pipe is then open?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let the pipes be **A**, **B** and **C** (waste pipe).

Total Work (LCM of 35, 15, 42) = **210 units**.

Efficiency: A = 6, B = 14, A + B − C = 5.

Efficiency of Waste Pipe C = (6 + 14) − 5 = **15 units/min**.

Time taken by C to empty = 210 ÷ 15 = **14 min**.

**∴ The correct answer is 14 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 
 **Pipe** **Time (min)** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 A (Filling) 35 210 6 
 B (Filling) 15 14 
 A + B − C 42 5 

⇒ Let efficiency of emptying pipe be **C**.

⇒ Total efficiency = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B − Efficiency of C

⇒ 5 = 6 + 14 − C

⇒ 5 = 20 − C

⇒ C = 20 − 5 = **15 units/min**

⇒ Time taken by pipe C to empty the cistern = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time = 210 ÷ 15 = 14 min

**∴ The correct answer is 14 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Net Efficiency Concept

For a cistern with inlet and outlet pipes, Net efficiency = ∑(Inlet efficiencies) − ∑(Outlet efficiencies). If net efficiency is positive, the tank fills; if negative, the tank empties.

Time and Work Relation

Time taken to complete a task is inversely proportional to efficiency: Time = Total Work ÷ Efficiency. In pipes and cisterns, capacity of the tank acts as the Total Work.</p

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 8 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 11 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill three-fourth of the tank?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net filling efficiency per minute = (1/8 − 1/11) = 3/88 of the tank.

Time to fill full tank = 88/3 minutes.

Time to fill 3/4th tank = (88/3) × (3/4) = 22 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 22 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling pipe time = 8 min, Emptying pipe time = 11 min.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = LCM of time taken; Efficiency = Work ÷ Time.

 
 **Pipe Type** **Time (min)** **Total Capacity (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 Inlet Pipe (+) 8 88 units +11 
 Outlet Pipe (−) 11 −8 

⇒ Combined efficiency of both pipes = 11 − 8 = 3 units/min.

⇒ Required work = 3/4 of Total Capacity = 3/4 × 88 = 66 units.

⇒ Time required = Required work ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Time = 66 ÷ 3 = 22 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 22 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Convention

Inlet pipes that fill the tank are taken as positive efficiency, while outlet pipes that empty the tank are taken as negative efficiency.

Net Time Formula

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B empties in y hours (y > x), net time to fill the tank = (xy) ÷ (y − x).

Work and Time Relationship

Total Work = Efficiency × Time. For a constant work, efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken.</p

questions.question: Two pipes can fill a cistern, individually, in 44 min and 84 min, respectively. There is a pipe located at the bottom of the cistern to empty it. Efficiency of **C** = 33 − (21 + 11) = 33 − 32 = **1 unit/min**.

Time taken by **C** to empty = 924 ÷ 1 = **924 min**.

**∴ The correct answer is 924 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling Pipe 1 = 44 min, Filling Pipe 2 = 84 min, Combined (with waste pipe) = 28 min.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Time × Efficiency

 
 **Pipe** **Time (min)** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 Pipe A 44 924 21 
 Pipe B 84 11 
 A + B − C 28 33 

⇒ Efficiency of Pipe A = 924 ÷ 44 = 21

⇒ Efficiency of Pipe B = 924 ÷ 84 = 11

⇒ Combined Efficiency (A + B − C) = 924 ÷ 28 = 33

⇒ 21 + 11 − Efficiency of C = 33

⇒ 32 − Efficiency of C = 33

⇒ Efficiency of C (Waste Pipe) = 32 − 33 = −1 (Negative sign denotes emptying)

⇒ Time to empty the cistern = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

**Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency**

Filling pipes have **positive efficiency**, while emptying or waste pipes have **negative efficiency**.

**LCM Method**

Always take the **Least Common Multiple** of individual time periods to assume a convenient **Total Work** value.</p

questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 18 days and B can complete it in 22 days. If they work on alternate days, starting with B on the first day, then in how many days will the work be finished?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(18, 22) = 198 units.

Efficiency: A = 11, B = 9.

2-day cycle (B+A) = 9 + 11 = 20 units.

In 9 cycles (18 days), work done = 9 × 20 = 180 units. Remaining = 18 units.

Day 19: B does 9 units. Remaining = 9 units. Day 20: A does 9/11 of work.

Total time = 18 + 1 + 9/11 = 19 9/11 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 9/11 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A finishes in 18 days, B finishes in 22 days. They work **alternately** starting with **B**.

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 A 18 198 11 
 B 22 9 

⇒ Work done in first 2 days (B then A) = 9 + 11 = 20 units.

⇒ Number of such 2-day cycles = 198 ÷ 20 = 9 cycles with remainder 18.

⇒ Days for 9 cycles = 9 × 2 = 18 days.

⇒ Remaining work = 198 − 180 = 18 units.

⇒ 19th day (B's turn): B completes 9 units. Remaining work = 18 − 9 = 9 units.

⇒ 20th day (A's turn): Time taken by A = 9 ÷ 11 days.

⇒ Total time = 18 + 1 + 9/11 = 19 9/11 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 9/11 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Work

In alternate day problems, always calculate the work done in one full cycle (e.g., 2 days if there are 2 people) and divide the total work by this cycle's efficiency.

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. If A takes T₁ days and B takes T₂ days, their efficiencies are in the ratio T₂ : T₁.</p

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill an empty cistern in 84 minutes and 36 minutes, respectively. Both Pipe A and Pipe B are opened together. After how much time should Pipe B be turned off so that the empty cistern is completely filled in a total of 42 minutes?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
**Total Work** (LCM of 84 and 36) = 252 units.

Efficiency of **Pipe A** = 252 ÷ 84 = 3 units/min.

Efficiency of **Pipe B** = 252 ÷ 36 = 7 units/min.

**Pipe A** works for the full 42 minutes: 3 × 42 = 126 units.

Remaining work for **Pipe B** = 252 − 126 = 126 units.

Time for **Pipe B** = 126 ÷ 7 = 18 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency**
 **Pipe A** 84 min 252 3
 **Pipe B** 36 min 7
**Given:**

Time taken by **Pipe A** = 84 min

Time taken by **Pipe B** = 36 min

Total time for cistern to fill = 42 min

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Pipe B** be closed after **x** minutes.

⇒ **Pipe A** works for the entire 42 minutes.

⇒ Work done by **Pipe A** in 42 minutes = 3 × 42 = 126 units

⇒ Remaining work to be filled by **Pipe B** = 252 − 126 = 126 units

⇒ Time for which **Pipe B** was open (x) = 126 ÷ 7

⇒ x = 18 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 18 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If a pipe fills a tank in T minutes, its efficiency is 1/T per minute.

Negative Work (Outlet Pipe)

If an outlet pipe (leak) is present, its efficiency is taken as negative during the total work calculation.

Total Work Calculation

Total Work = Time × Combined Efficiency. Always use the LCM of individual times to assume a convenient value for total capacity.</p

questions.question: A can finish a work in 2 days and B can do the same work in 52 days. B worked alone for 26 days and left the job. In how many days can A alone finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work (LCM of 2, 52) = **52 units**.

Efficiency of **B** = 52 ÷ 52 = **1 unit/day**.

Work done by **B** in 26 days = 26 × 1 = **26 units**.

Remaining work = 52 − 26 = **26 units**.

Efficiency of **A** = 52 ÷ 2 = **26 units/day**.

Time for **A** to finish = 26 ÷ 26 = **1 day**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 day.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **A** = 2 days, Time taken by **B** = 52 days.

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 **A** 2 52 26 
 **B** 52 1 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done by **B** in 26 days = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Work done by **B** = 1 × 26 = **26 units**

⇒ Remaining Work = Total Work − Work Done

⇒ Remaining Work = 52 − 26 = **26 units**

⇒ Time taken by **A** alone = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of A

⇒ Time taken by **A** = 26 ÷ 26 = **1 day**

**∴ The correct answer is 1 day.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency Concept

**Efficiency** is inversely proportional to the **time** taken to complete the work (Efficiency = Work ÷ Time).

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed in the **ratio of work done** or the **ratio of efficiencies** if they work for the same duration.

Pipes and Cisterns

This follows the same logic where filling a tank is **positive work** and a leak (emptying) is **negative work**.</p

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 19 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 21 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill two-third of the tank?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net filling efficiency per minute = 1/19 − 1/21 = (21 − 19) / (19 × 21) = 2 / 399

Time to fill full tank = 399 / 2 minutes

Time to fill 2/3rd tank = (399 / 2) × (2 / 3) = 133 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 133 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time = 19 minutes, Emptying time = 21 minutes.

**Formula Used:** Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 **Pipe Type** **Time (min)** **Total Capacity (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 **Filling Pipe** 19 399 +21 
 **Emptying Pipe** 21 −19 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Net efficiency of both pipes = 21 − 19 = 2 units/min

⇒ Required work = 2/3 of Total Capacity = (2/3) × 399 = 266 units

⇒ Required time = Required work ÷ Net efficiency

⇒ Required time = 266 ÷ 2 = 133 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 133 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Net Rate of Flow

When one pipe fills (rate x) and another empties (rate y), the combined rate is (1/x − 1/y) per unit time.

Pipes and Cisterns Logic

Inlet pipes contribute positive work (+) while Outlet pipes contribute negative work (−) towards filling the tank.

Partial Filling

Time taken to fill 'k' fraction of a tank = (k × Total Capacity) ÷ Net Efficiency.</p

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill an empty cistern in 72 minutes and 76 minutes, respectively. Both Pipe A and Pipe B are opened together. After how much time should Pipe B be turned off so that the empty cistern is completely filled in a total of 54 minutes?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
**Pipe A** works for the entire **54 minutes**.

Work done by **Pipe A** in 54 min = 54 ÷ 72 = 3/4 of the total capacity.

Remaining work to be done by **Pipe B** = 1 − 3/4 = 1/4.

Time for which **Pipe B** was open = (1/4) × 76 = 19 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **Pipe A** = 72 min; Time taken by **Pipe B** = 76 min; Total time = 54 min.

 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency**
 **Pipe A** 72 min 1368 units 19
 **Pipe B** 76 min 18
**Formula:** Total Work = (Efficiency × Time)

⇒ Let **Pipe B** be closed after **'x' minutes**.

⇒ Total work = (Efficiency of A × 54) + (Efficiency of B × x)

⇒ 1368 = (19 × 54) + (18 × x)

⇒ 1368 = 1026 + 18x

⇒ 18x = 1368 − 1026

⇒ 18x = 342

⇒ x = 342 ÷ 18 = 19 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Efficiency

The efficiency of a pipe is inversely proportional to the time taken to fill or empty a cistern. Efficiency = Total Capacity ÷ Time.

Combined Work Formula

If two pipes A and B can fill a tank in x and y hours respectively, their 1 hour's work is (1/x + 1/y). Combined time = (xy)/(x + y).

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipe efficiency is positive (+), while outlet (leakage) pipe efficiency is negative (−). Net work = Σ Efficiency × Time.</p
